sentences.text: The name Adynomosaurus combines Greek words for 'weak shoulder lizard' to describe its underdeveloped shoulder blade and likely weaker musculature.
The species name arcanus means 'secret' or 'occult', referring to the sparse and uninformative hadrosaur fossil record in the South-Central Pyrenean Basin.
As a lambeosaur, Adynomosaurus had a long skull with a beak, complex teeth, and a nasal cranial crest filled with hollow passages.
The tooth crowns of this dinosaur are approximately three times taller than they are wide.
Adynomosaurus was anatomically indistinguishable from other hadrosaurid dinosaurs in many aspects, such as vertebrae, humerus, femur, tibia, and metatarsals.
The most distinctive feature of Adynomosaurus anatomy is its scapula, which has unique traits exclusive to it among hadrosaurids.
Adynomosaurus was first discovered in 2012 and formally named in 2019 as the species Adynomosaurus arcanus.
The fossil site of Adynomosaurus was discovered in 2012 in a wheat field in the village of Basturs, Catalonia.
Remains of Adynomosaurus were found in Catalonia, Spain.
Adynomosaurus fossils are known from the Conques Formation of the Tremp Group.
Adynomosaurus was a quadrupedal animal capable of walking bipedally on its hind legs.
Based on modern crocodylian myology, researchers surmise that the reduced scapulae of Adynomosaurus meant reduced arm musculature.
The Conques Formation ecosystem represents one of only two known instances where a rhabdodontid (Pareisactus) coexisted with hadrosaurs.
Isotope analysis of dinosaur eggshells indicated a wet environment with a mean air temperature of 21 C.
Marine microfossils, including red algae and echinoderms, were found deposited in the river and marsh environment.
Adynomosaurus was originally described as a member of the Lambeosaurinae subfamily, but its specific relationships remain unresolved.
Some studies suggest Adynomosaurus is outside Lambeosaurinae and is a non-hadrosaurid hadrosauroid closely related to Nanningosaurus.
In a phylogenetic analysis, Adynomosaurus emerged in a soft polytomy with the genera Aralosaurus, Canardia, Jaxartosaurus, Tsintaosaurus, and Pararhabdodon as the base of the family.
Adynomosaurus belongs to the subfamily Arenysaurini.
Adynomosaurus lived during the Early Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, specifically between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
Adynomosaurus lived in a diverse coastal estuary ecosystem consisting of meandering rivers and mud flats in what is now Europe.
The formation is considered to represent a tide-dominated delta adjacent to meandering river channels influenced by interior tides.
It is debated whether Adynomosaurus belongs within Hadrosauridae, with some studies placing it in Tsintaosaurini and others maintaining its position as a lambeosaurine.
It is unknown whether the replacement of local herbivores by lambeosaurs was due to direct competition or environmental changes creating a void for them.
